items.title: Karnataka seeks to contest Cauvery water allocation, cites changing hydrological conditions
items.summary: Karnataka has signalled to the Supreme Court that it may seek to reopen the Cauvery water-sharing allocation, citing “inequitable allocation” and “changed circumstances” caused by changing hydrological conditions. According to a report by The Hindu , the state made the submission on October 7, in its response to Tamil Nadu’s application over the backlog in Cauvery water releases. Karnataka said it reserved the right to seek a reconsideration of the allocation made by the Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal and modified by the Supreme Court in 2018. Karnataka’s 40-page response, filed by advocate Nishanth Patil and settled by senior advocate Mohan Katarki, referred to the legal principle of rebus sic stantibus, under which arrangements can be revisited when circumstances underlying them have substantially changed. “In view of the looming inequity, the state of Karnataka reserves its right to apply in the changed circumstances for reopening of the inequitable allocation in the Award of Tribunal read with judgment of the Supreme Court. The normal practice is that the water allocations are periodically revisited,” the response said. The report said Karnataka also cited the Union government
